Title: LocoMamba: Vision-driven locomotion via end-to-end deep reinforcement learning with Mamba - ScienceDirect
# Full length article LocoMamba: Vision-driven locomotion via end-to-end deep reinforcement learning with Mamba. First vision-driven Mamba-based cross-modal DRL for quadruped locomotion control. Mamba fusion backbone enables efficient long-horizon control with near-linear cost. Applying deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to quadrupedal robots is promising for obstacle negotiation, terrain locomotion, and real-world deployment. In this paper, LocoMamba, a vision-driven end-to-end DRL framework that uses Mamba as a selective state–space model (SSM) backbone, is introduced to enable efficient quadrupedal locomotion. **State-of-the-art LocoMamba:** To the best of our knowledge, this is the first vision-driven cross-modal DRL framework for quadrupedal locomotion that utilizes the selective state–space model Mamba as the fusion backbone, enabling foresightful and efficient control. **Effective proprioception and depth encoders:** A compact input representation is proposed in which an MLP embeds proprioceptive states and a CNN patchifies depth images into spatial tokens tailored for Mamba-based fusion. **Efficient cross-modal Mamba fusion backbone:** The encoded tokens are fused from proprioception states and depth images using stacked Mamba layers via selective state–space scanning, achieving near-linear time and memory scaling. **Robust end-to-end RL training scheme:** The policy is trained with PPO using Mamba-fused cross-modal features, complemented by terrain and appearance randomization and an obstacle-density curriculum. Section 3 presents the LocoMamba methodology, including the problem formulation, proprioception and depth encoders, and the Mamba fusion backbone with training objectives. Research on quadrupedal locomotion has evolved along two principal paradigms: model-based optimal control and learning-based approaches. **RQ1 (SOTA performance).** Does *LocoMamba*, which fuses proprioception and depth with Mamba SSM backbone, achieve better locomotion performance than SOTA, as measured by return, collision times, and distance moved? This paper presented *LocoMamba*, a vision-driven cross-modal reinforcement learning framework for quadrupedal locomotion. The method embeds proprioceptive state with a lightweight MLP and patchifies depth images with a compact CNN, then fuses the resulting tokens using stacked Mamba selective state–space layers. ### Learning vision-guided quadrupedal locomotion end-to-end with cross-modal transformers. ### Reinforcement learning for robust parameterized locomotion control of bipedal robots. End-to-end reinforcement learning (RL) for motion control trains policies directly from sensor inputs to motor commands, enabling unified controllers for different robots and tasks.

results.content:
Title: LocoMamba: Vision-Driven Locomotion via End-to-End Deep Reinforcement Learning with Mamba
We introduce LocoMamba, a vision-driven cross-modal DRL framework built on selective state-space models, specifically leveraging Mamba, that achieves near-linear-time sequence modeling, effectively captures long-range dependencies, and enables efficient training with longer sequences. Second, stacked Mamba layers fuse these tokens via near-linear-time selective scanning, reducing latency and memory footprint, remaining robust to token length and image resolution, and providing an inductive bias that mitigates overfitting. Despite this, current cross-modal fusion architectures face critical limitations: recurrent models suffer from vanishing gradients and poor long-horizon modeling, hierarchical designs complicate optimization, and Transformer-based models incur quadratic computational and memory costs with sequence length, constraining resolution and training efficiency. To address these challenges, this work introduces LocoMamba, a vision-driven end-to-end DRL framework that leverages the selective state-space model Mamba as a fusion backbone. LocoMamba encodes proprioceptive states and depth images into compact tokens, which are fused via stacked Mamba layers using selective state-space scanning with near-linear time complexity. The policy is trained with Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) under terrain and appearance randomization and an obstacle-density curriculum, using a compact, state-centric reward that balances task progress, energy efficiency, and safety. LocoMamba represents the first application of Mamba-based cross-modal fusion to quadrupedal locomotion, enabling efficient, foresightful control with strong generalization and faster convergence under limited compute. Proprioception and depth are encoded into tokens by MLP/CNN, fused by a Mamba SSM backbone, and optimized with PPO. Proprioception and depth are encoded into tokens by MLP/CNN, fused by a Mamba SSM backbone, and optimized with PPO.\*\* ## Methodology and Architecture Design LocoMamba’s architecture is structured into three end-to-end trainable components: input encoding, cross-modal fusion via Mamba, and policy optimization. The fusion backbone consists of stacked Mamba selective state-space model (SSM) layers, which process the token sequence through input-dependent, recurrent state updates. Each Mamba layer maintains a hidden state \(x\_{t,k}\) and computes state transitions using input-gated parameters \(\bar{A}\_{t,k}, \bar{B}\_{t,k}, \bar{C}\_{t,k}, \bar{D}\_{t,k}\), enabling selective scanning that scales near-linearly with sequence length. After processing through \(L\_m\) Mamba layers with residual connections and layer normalization, the final fused features are obtained via modality-aware pooling: the proprioceptive token and mean-pooled visual tokens are concatenated and passed through a small MLP to produce the control feature \(h\_t\).

results.content: State-of-the-art LocoMamba: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first vision-driven cross-modal DRL framework for quadrupedal locomotion that utilizes the selective state-space model Mamba as the fusion backbone, enabling foresightful and efficient control. Efficient cross-modal Mamba fusion backbone: Encoded tokens from proprioception and depth are fused using stacked Mamba layers via selective state-space scanning, achieving near-linear time and memory scaling. State-of-the-art LocoMamba: To the best of our knowledge, this is the first vision-driven cross-modal DRL framework for quadrupedal locomotion that utilizes the selective state-space model Mamba as the fusion backbone, enabling foresightful and efficient control. Efficient cross-modal Mamba fusion backbone: The encoded tokens are fused from proprioception states and depth images using stacked Mamba layers via selective state-space scanning, achieving near-linear time and memory scaling. Taken together, these results support RQ3: the Mamba-based backbone improves optimization dynamics under the same training budget and confers efficiency benefits that translate into faster learning and stronger final performance when cross-modal fusion is used.
